key_insight: Reason through a task once, then reuse its solution instead of asking an LLM to solve it from scratch each time. CPU-ARC turns reasoning into CPU-executable caches that can handle new instances with little LLM involvement.
problem_solved: LLMs often repeat reasoning for similar tasks because they combine discovering a solution with executing it, creating avoidable computation and model usage.
method: Use LLM reasoning to establish a reusable approach to a task.
Construct a robust, CPU-executable agentic reasoning cache (ARC) from that reasoning.
Apply the cached solution to new problem instances with minimal LLM involvement.
impact: Reusing executable reasoning could reduce repeated LLM computation and make recurring AI workflows more efficient. The provided abstract excerpt does not include quantitative performance results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM reasoning → executable ARC → CPU execution on new inputs.
Side-by-side workflows: reasoning from scratch each time versus reasoning once and reusing.
One-to-many diagram showing a single cached solution serving multiple problem instances.
CPU and LLM icons highlighting the shift from model-based reasoning to cached execution.
paper_title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
paper_authors: Peter Belcak, Greg Heinrich, Saurav Muralidharan, Shizhe Diao, Pavlo Molchanov
